_comment: Recurring CI/PR monitoring as a ROUTINE instead of as repeated polling inside a long session.
Why this template exists: in one retro window, 113 CI/PR status checks were issued from inside
sessions that had already grown past $50 of cost. Each of those checks re-read the whole
accumulated context to ask a question whose answer is three lines of JSON — the advisor's
fat-session rule names exactly this and recommends 'move recurring monitoring to a routine that
reads state with a fresh small context'.
Both steps are `command`, not `ai-prompt`, on purpose: no model is invoked at all, so the check
that used to cost a full context re-read now costs zero tokens. Read the answers in the routine's
run history on the Routines page.
Install it against a project with (`swarmery api` signs the request with the link token:
the daemon takes a write that carries no browser Origin only with link auth):
swarmery api POST /api/routines --data @<this file with _comment removed and projectId set>
The cron is deliberately half-hourly rather than minute-by-minute: this replaces a human-paced
'is it green yet?', and a tighter schedule would recreate the polling it is meant to remove.
name: CI and PR watch

steps.name: CI runs on the default branch
steps.command: gh run list --limit 10 --json workflowName,headBranch,status,conclusion,url --jq '[.[] | select(.conclusion != "success" and .conclusion != "skipped")] | if length == 0 then "CI: all recent runs green" else "CI NOT GREEN:\n" + (map("  \(.workflowName) on \(.headBranch): \(.status)/\(.conclusion // "running") \(.url)") | join("\n")) end'

steps.name: Open PRs and their checks
steps.command: gh pr list --state open --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup --jq 'if length == 0 then "PRs: none open" else map("  #\(.number) \(.title)\(if .isDraft then " [draft]" else "" end): \(.mergeStateStatus) — checks \([.statusCheckRollup[]? | select(.conclusion != null and .conclusion != "SUCCESS" and .conclusion != "NEUTRAL" and .conclusion != "SKIPPED")] | length) failing") | join("\n") end'
